reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports the superior OER activity of the epitaxial high-entropy perovskite over its single-B-site parents and reports simultaneous valence changes across multiple cations, which underpins the cooperative redox premise. However, the evidence does not address the proposed physical mixture baseline or the specific claim that d-orbital coupling is the governing mechanism, leaving those premises unsupported.
premises: High-entropy perovskite oxide outperforms single-B-site parent compounds for OER
Epitaxial growth ensures identical morphology and surface termination for comparison
Multiple transition metals in the high-entropy oxide exhibit simultaneous valence changes during OER
The enhanced activity is attributed to a synergistic electronic effect from multiple active sites
The physical mixture baseline lacks a contiguous lattice for effective orbital coupling
